chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad from someone else from Aban from Ibn al-Mundhir who said:
Loneliness was mentioned in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so he said: Shall I not inform you of something that if you say it, you will not feel lonely at night or during the day?

In the name of Allah and by Allah, and I relied upon Allah, and indeed whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him. Allah accomplishes His command. Allah has decreed a measure for everything. O Allah, make me under Your wing and in Your shelter, and make me in Your security and in Your protection.
So he said: It reached us that a man recited it for thirty years and left it for one night, so a scorpion stung him.

key_terms.قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْ‏ءٍ قَدْ: Allah has decreed a measure for everything

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for protection against loneliness and what is its significance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes this specific dhikr as a spiritual shield against *wahshah* (spiritual loneliness or alienation), linking inner tranquility to consistent reliance on Allah’s decree (*qadr*). The narration’s concluding anecdote regarding the scorpion sting serves as a practical validation of the dhikr’s efficacy, illustrating how even a single night of neglect can expose one to physical and spiritual vulnerability, a theme deeply resonant in Shia devotional practices.
